To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) gaze direction influences the facial and physiological reactions to others' facial displays, (ii) the effect of gaze direction depends on the emotion displayed by the sender and on the observer's sex and (iii) the effect of emotion is mediated by the observer's self-relevance appraisal.
the impact of facial expressions of emotion on facial reactions of observers is influenced by gaze direction and gender.

(1) the presence of gaze direction in the sender of facial expression affects the magnitude of facial electromyographic reactions of observers, and (2) these effects depend on the nature of the facial expression and gender of the observer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how people respond to others' emotional expressions and whether the responses are affected by the gaze direction of the sender.
the processes underlying interpersonal matching of facial expression.
the question of whether facial reactions of observers to others' facial displays are influenced by the perceived gaze behavior of the sender.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processes underlying interpersonal matching of facial responses to dynamic facial expressions depend on the specific nature of the emotion and the context in which it is expressed.
the facial expressions of emotion and the direction of gaze of the sender of the facial expression are important factors that influence the facial expressions of the receiver.
gaze direction is a contextual cue that can modulate the intensity of the emotional response to facial expressions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
facial expressions of emotions are processed in a complex way that depends on the social context, and that the processing of facial expressions of emotions is modulated by the gender of the observer.
gaze direction and emotional expressions are important social cues that influence facial responses to others.
the self-relevance appraisal is a crucial mechanism for interpersonal matching of emotion expressions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
facial mimicry is a dynamic process, influenced by both the sender's emotional state and the perceiver's self-relevance appraisal.
gaze direction and emotional expressions have a differential impact on the observer's autonomic and RFR responses.
the impact of gaze behavior and emotional facial expressions on observers is moderated by individual differences in self-relevance appraisal.
